slot.brief: Use R = ρL/A with volume conserved: a wire is stretched to n times its length; ask the factor by which resistance increases.

stem: A wire of resistance $2\ \Omega$ is stretched uniformly to three times its original length without changing its volume. By what factor does its resistance increase?

verdicts.working: With volume constant, stretching to 3 times the length makes the area one-third. Since R ∝ L/A, the resistance factor is 3 ÷ (1/3) = 9.

working:
$LA=L'A'$, so $A'=A/3$.
$R'/R=(L'/L)(A/A')=3\times3=9$. Independent check: With volume constant, stretching to 3 times the length makes the area one-third. Since R ∝ L/A, the resistance factor is 3 ÷ (1/3) = 9.
